deepDive.markdownContent:
## ⚙️ Consistent Hashing Ring & Layer 4 vs Layer 7 Routing

Traditional modulo hashing (`hash(key) % N`) causes catastrophic cache invalidation when a server joins or leaves: nearly 100% of keys remap to new nodes. **Consistent Hashing** maps both servers and data keys onto a shared $2^{32} - 1$ circular ring space, guaranteeing that adding or removing a node only reassigns $K/N$ keys on average.

```architecture
{
  "view": "high-level",
  "title": "Consistent Hashing Ring with Virtual Nodes",
  "nodes": [
    { "id": "ring", "label": "2^32 Integer Hash Ring", "type": "service" },
    { "id": "nodeA", "label": "Node A (vnodes: A1, A2, A3)", "type": "database" },
    { "id": "nodeB", "label": "Node B (vnodes: B1, B2, B3)", "type": "database" },
    { "id": "key", "label": "Incoming Key Hash", "type": "client" }
  ],
  "edges": [
    { "from": "key", "to": "ring", "label": "1. Hash(Key)" },
    { "from": "ring", "to": "nodeA", "label": "2. Walk Clockwise to Next VNode" }
  ]
}
```

### 🌀 Virtual Nodes (VNodes) for Uniform Load Distribution

In a naive ring with only 3 physical nodes, non-uniform hash distribution creates hot spots where one server absorbs 60% of all traffic. Systems like Amazon DynamoDB and Discord resolve this using **Virtual Nodes (VNodes)**:

- Each physical server is assigned multiple token positions (e.g. 100–256 virtual nodes) uniformly across the ring.
- Higher-capacity servers receive proportionally more tokens.
- When a server crashes, its virtual tokens are evenly dispersed among all remaining physical nodes rather than dumping 100% of its load onto a single immediate neighbor.

### ⚖️ Layer 4 vs Layer 7 Load Balancing

| Attribute | Layer 4 (Transport / TCP/UDP) | Layer 7 (Application / HTTP/gRPC) |
|---|---|---| 
| **Inspection Depth** | IP packet header & TCP port only | Full HTTP request (path, headers, cookies, payload) |
| **Throughput & CPU** | Millions of packets/sec with zero copy | High CPU cost for TLS termination & HTTP parsing |
| **Routing Capabilities** | Round-robin, least connections, IP hash | Path routing (`/api/v2`), gRPC multiplexing, cookie stickiness |
| **Common Tech** | AWS NLB, Linux IPVS, HAProxy (TCP mode) | AWS ALB, Envoy, NGINX, Traefik |

questions.title: Consistent Hashing Node Membership Changes
questions.prompt: What is the primary advantage of Consistent Hashing over standard modulo hashing (hash(K) mod N) when scaling cache cluster nodes?

options.text: It encrypts cache keys using AES-256 before hashing.
options.explanation: Consistent hashing is an allocation algorithm, not encryption.

options.text: Adding or removing a node only remaps K/N keys rather than invalidating almost all cached keys across the entire cluster.
options.explanation: Correct! Only 1/N keys are remapped on cluster membership changes.

rubric.excellent: Identifies minimal key remapping (K/N keys) and prevention of cache stampede on node scale events.
rubric.gap: Confuses hashing with encryption.

questions.sampleSolution: Consistent hashing minimizes key remapping during node additions/removals, re-allocating only K/N keys.
questions.explanation: Standard modulo hashing remaps ~100% of keys when N changes, causing massive cache invalidation.

interviewProblems.title: Stateful Voice Socket Load Balancer
interviewProblems.scenarioPrompt: You are designing the gateway load balancer for a real-time voice chat application serving 10,000,000 concurrent WebSocket connections. When a backend voice server crashes or scales up, how do you minimize connection drops and avoid server overload?

dimensions.name: Layer 4 vs Layer 7 Selection
dimensions.description: Using L4 Maglev/IPVS for socket throughput and L7 Envoy for HTTP routing.

dimensions.name: Consistent Ring Virtual Nodes
dimensions.description: Using virtual nodes (vnodes) to prevent traffic hotspots.

interviewProblems.sampleDefense: Use Layer 4 Maglev consistent hashing for incoming TCP WebSocket handshakes. Use virtual nodes (vnodes=256) per voice server to evenly distribute connections and ensure scaling up or down only migrates 1/N connections.
commonPitfalls: Using simple round-robin which breaks sticky WebSocket sessions.
